current_focus.summary: The project owner (GitHub saariuslystoned) chose 'Apply it' on 2026-10-08 when asked whether to stop the inventory CLI from sending its token to an endpoint set in project config. Project config travels with the working directory, so it may still set site and read context but no longer the token's destination. No publication, deployment or merge is authorized by this choice.

decisions.choice: Use zod/mini (zod's small edition, same validation core) in the plugin and the Store Connect protocol it imports; build the bundle from the plugin directory so zod/mini is bundled. Hosted service keeps full zod. Hand-written checks rejected: a few KB smaller but means rewriting every rule by hand with no guarantee of identical behaviour.

decisions.choice: No. The token goes only to an endpoint from --endpoint, DINKUS_INVENTORY_ENDPOINT, or user config (including a user-config profile). An endpoint from project config, directly or through a profile, exits 4 with untrusted_endpoint before any request. Project config may still set site and read context. commands resolve replays to the endpoint saved in the local pending record. This amends the locked v1 docs/CLI-SPEC.md.

decisions.question: May dinkus-inventory send DINKUS_INVENTORY_TOKEN to an endpoint that came from project config (.dinkuskit/inventory.json)?
decisions.rationale: Same rule as the Commerce and Payments CLIs after the ClawSweeper credential-routing finding: a cloned repository's config must not choose which host receives the bearer token.
